children: shares fell about 2% in morning trading Friday even after the company completed a cross-country autonomous flight, showing that investors remain cautious around its plans for automated aviation.

A converted Cessna Caravan traveled 3,199 miles from California to North Carolina with no control inputs from the onboard safety pilot. The aircraft handled taxiing, takeoffs, navigation and landings while teams supervised the journey remotely from California and South Carolina.

The trip covered busy airspace, mountainous areas and routes affected by severe weather. Joby said the test showed its autonomous system could operate across varied conditions and support potential uses including freight, emergency response and defense logistics.

The milestone comes as Joby shares remain down more than 50% this year. The aircraft will then start its westbound return trip. Separately, Chief Executive JoeBen Bevirt sold 606,667 shares on Sept. 15 at an average price of $6.19, according to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing. The transaction involved shares held through the Joby Trust and was made under a trading plan adopted in March.

title: Joby Stock Falls Despite Landmark Autonomous Flight Across America
